newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Thai stocks ended lower in active trade on Tuesday after investors sold stocks and took profits amid uncertainty how long heavy gains made on Monday could be sustained, brokers said.

The SET index, which fluctuated after the opening and moved steadily in the negative zone during the afternoon session, closed at 1,085.64-point, down 13.37 points, on 6.7 billion baht trade. The SET-50 index slipped 1.05 points to 83.51.
"The market fell because of profit-taking after it rose heavily yesterday. Investors also didn't response to the lower inflation figures released in the afternoon," said a broker.
The SET index closed 4.87 percent higher on Monday after investors bought on news Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa had late on Friday called a snap election on November 17.
News that September inflation rose less than in August failed to move the market.

"Investors seemed not to care much about inflation figures. Speculative investors sold and tested the market at the same time whether the heavy gains on Monday would last long or not," said Kasem Prunratanamala of James Capel Asia.
The Commerce Ministry said on Tuesday Thai consumer price index rose 4.6 percent year-on-year in September and 0.1 percent month-on-month.
"Thailand's current account deficit and exports are major concerns among investors at present," Kasem said.

The Thai central bank said exports rose a marginal 2.9 percent year-on-year during January-July against 26.5 percent growth seen in the same period in 1995. Current account deficit was 30.8 billion baht in July from 35.4 billion in June.

Bank and finance issues topped the active list in terms of value. General Finance ranked first on the list, rising 3.50 baht to 72.50. Siam Commercial Bank slipped eight to 244 and TelecomAsia rose two to 53.50.
